Troubleshooting

Quick solutions for common problems.

Installation

“pip: command not found”

  • Install Python from python.org

  • During installation, check “Add Python to PATH”

“No module named ‘PyQt5’”

pip install -r requirements.txt

This installs all required packages.

Files

“Can’t open my FITS file”

  1. Check if file is actually FITS format (.fits or .fit extension)

  2. Ensure file contains INSTRUME header keyword identifying it as MUSE, ALMA, MIRI, or NIRSpec

  3. Try “File → Advanced → Choose HDU” for files with multiple layers

Display

“Image looks too bright/dark”

Click Color Scale button. Use Auto Scale for automatic adjustment, or drag vmin/vmax sliders.

“Data is invisible”

  • Check wavelength slider position

  • Make sure you’re looking at a bright wavelength

  • Try adjusting vmin/vmax

“Performance is slow”

Close other applications. For large files: - Use smaller wavelength ranges - Analyze just one region instead of full cube - Reduce zoom level or work with sub-regions

Analysis

“Spectrum has too much noise”

Right-click spectrum → Rebin to combine adjacent pixels.

“Can’t see my spectral line”

  1. Check you’re at the right wavelength

  2. Try subtracting continuum first (makes lines clearer)

  3. Adjust intensity range (vmin/vmax)

“Gaussian fit is bad”

  1. Select a narrower wavelength range around the line

  2. Subtract continuum first

  3. Make sure you’re fitting actual data (not noise)

“Many pixels failed to fit”

  1. Adjust quality threshold (accept lower-quality fits)

  2. Use a wider wavelength range

  3. Try with a different fitting method

Export

“Can’t open exported file”

Export as FITS format (most compatible). Test with DS9 first.

General

Something else is broken

  1. Check the FAQ section

  2. Try restarting the application

  3. Verify your data file is valid (open in another tool like DS9)

Contact the development team if the problem persists.
